newsitem.title: USA: Senate approves tax cut legislation.
newsitem.headline: Senate approves tax cut legislation.

text.p: The Senate approved a five-year tax cut package Friday, a day after the House passed its version.

The Senate voted 80-18 to approve a bill to provide a $77 billion net tax cut over five years. Senate and House negotiators will meet in coming weeks to work out differences in the two bills so that one final bill can be sent to the president.

The legislation would implement the tax part of the balanced-budget agreement reached between congressional leaders and the White House last month. The Senate bill would provide a $500 tax credit for each child under age 17 and require the credit be deposited in a type of Individual Retirement Account for education for children aged 13 to 16.
It offered tax relief for college education costs and a capital gains tax cut to 20 percent from the maximum 28 percent rate for individuals. The bill expanded Individual Retirement Accounts.

The bill would gradually raise the threshold for imposing the estate tax to $1 million in 2006 from 600,000 now, and immediately exclude $1 million from tax when a family-owned business comprised more than 50 percent of the estate.

The bill would also raise $66 billion over five years in revenues by increasing taxes or eliminating tax breaks. Measures involved include airline ticket taxes and passenger fees, a 20-cent per pack increase in the cigarette tax, and a gradual reduction in the ethanol subsidy starting in 2001.
